provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 3547 MCHARD RD, PEARLAND, TX, 77581

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Fire Extinguishers Serviced: Four fire extinguishers were observed needing to be serviced.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Extinguishers Serviced (26 TAC §746.5307(b))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Screen time was observed being used in the school age room during nap time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Fire Inspection: The most recent fire inspection report was not available for review during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Fire Inspection (26 TAC §746.5103)

occurrences.finding: Administering Medication - Not After Expiration date: Seizure medication for a child was observed to have expired on 6/7/2026.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Administering Medication - Not After Expiration date (26 TAC §746.3805(b)(3))

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Cleaning supplies were observed accessible to children in two bathrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials (26 TAC §746.3407(13))

occurrences.finding: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Never Allow Toddlers to Sleep or Walk With Bottles and Training Cups: Two children between the ages of two to three were observed walking while drinking from a bottle and a sippy cup.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Never Allow Toddlers to Sleep or Walk With Bottles and Training Cups (26 TAC §746.2505(4)(C))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Knows in Charge: There was no caregiver designated in charge before the director arrived for the day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Knows in Charge (26 TAC §746.1013(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Emergency Preparedness Plans: The emergency preparedness plan was not present in the parent provided operational policies.  This was corrected when the director added the complete emergency preparedness plan to the operational policies.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Emergency Preparedness Plans (26 TAC §746.501(a)(24))

occurrences.finding: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met: There were eight infants 12-18 months being supervised by one caregiver when the required ratio was five infants 12-18 months to one caregiver.   This was corrected when the owner added another caregiver to the ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met (26 TAC §746.1613(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Based upon the information obtained, the operation did not notify Child Care Regulation of a child who obtained an injury that required medical treatment within the required time frame.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based upon the information obtained, a caregiver did not maintain adequate supervision needed for an infant during water activities. As a result, the infant drank the sprinkler water.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Used According to Manufacturer's Instructions: Based upon the information obtained, the operation did not use play equipment according to manufacturer's instructions.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Used According to Manufacturer's Instructions (26 TAC §746.4601(2))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Based upon the information obtained, the operation did not notify Child Care Regulation of a child who required medical treatment by a Health-Care Professional within the required time frame.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Fire Inspection Report, Including Written Approval for Above/Below Ground Level Care: Documentation of the most recent fire inspection report was not available for review upon request.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Fire Inspection Report, Including Written Approval for Above/Below Ground Level Care (26 TAC §746.801(11))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: During the inspection, an individual was observed with direct access to children and the operation has not obtained an eligibility notification back from CBCU stating the person could be present.     Note: The individual left the facility during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 1 out of 3 children's files evaluated did not contain an updated immunization record.    Note: This was corrected at inspection when the provider obtained the udpated shot record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: I observed disinfectant wipes on the floor in the restroom which was accessible to children.     Note: The provider removed the cleaning wipes during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: During an inspection at the center on May 8th, 2023 a fire inspection had not been conducted at the center since March 28th, 2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: A child's head was completely covered during the follow up inspection in the toddler room.    Note: The provider corected this during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A child in the older pre-k classroom did not wash their hands after toileting.    Note: This was discussed and corrected during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: A caregiver did not know the number of children in the classroom during the inspection. The caregiver stated there were 18 children and there were only 17.    Note: Discussed with the provider all caregivers must know how many children are in the class at all times.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §746.1203(2))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: A broken soap dispenser was observed in the Pre-School classroom and the light in the restroom was not turning on in the Pre-School 2 when the light switch was flipped on.    Note: The operation corrected this during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Must Use for Each Child in When Transporting and be Properly Installed: Based upon the information obtained there is sufficient evidence to support the operation was transporting children with no car seats.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Must Use for Each Child in When Transporting and be Properly Installed (26 TAC §746.5607(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: Based upon the information obtained, there was sufficient evidence to support the operation did not maintain a transportation log showing the 3-year-old children that were being transported and it was not kept in the vehicle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Information About Facility: The operation did not keep the information showing the facility name and phone number inside the vehicle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Information About Facility (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Supplies Not Expired: The first aid kit in the vehicle used to transport children contained expired alcohol wipes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Supplies Not Expired (26 TAC §746.4003(b))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: 11 children were in the van upon arriving at the daycare center and only 10 children were showing on the transportation list.    Note: The driver corrected this during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: The sign in and out log for the pre-k classroom only had 5 children signed in when there were 19 children accounted for in the classroom.    Note: This was corrected during the inspection when the caregiver signed the rest of the children in.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver was observed in the pre-k classroom caring for children as they were using the restroom and preparing for naptime.    Note: The caregiver left the operation during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: 3 Infant feeding instructions had not been signed and dated within the last 30 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Napping Floor Mats Marked with Sleeping Side Distinguished: During walk-through it was observed 2 children laying on incorrect color side for napping mats. They were sleeping on  Floor side  instead of the  Sleeping side .
occurrences.violation_type_title: Napping Floor Mats Marked with Sleeping Side Distinguished (26 TAC §746.4503(c))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: While conducting walk-through I observed 3 classrooms where the children were not signed-in.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: During walk-through it was observed a spray bottle of Bleach located on a shelf next  children s cup. It was accessible to children. Note: the Director removed the spray bottle during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: Health Sanitation Inspection was not available for review during Inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: While conducting walk-through I observed 3 changing mats that were torn ,and cannot be properly cleared.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: While reviewing 6 staff files the following topics were missing :  PREVENTION AND RESPONSE TO FOOD ALLERGIES, STORAGE OF HAZARDOUS MATERIALS AND BIO-CONTAMINANTS,   EMERGENCY PREPARATION.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The operation failed to practice good judgment by allowing a child in care to disengage the emergency release button for the child safety alarm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: Based upon the findings from the DFPS Investigation, there is sufficient evidence to support neglectful supervision of a child in care has occurred at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Based upon the DFPS Investigation, the director failed to ensure that proper training had been completed and did not ensure the driver was following policies.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Based upon the findings from the DFPS Investigation, a person was allowed to transport children prior to completing the required 2 hours of Transportation Safety Training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children: A caregiver did not walk the van to account for all children accurately when exiting from the vehicle which resulted in a child being left on the van.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children (26 TAC §746.5605(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended: Based on the DFPS investigation, a child was left unattended on a van by a caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended (26 TAC §746.5605(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: Based on the DFPS investigation, the operation did not maintain supervision of a child who was left alone on the van for approximately 40 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))
